sectionsUsed: JLS SE 25, 3.10.7 Escape Sequences: Java string literals support the named escapes b, t, n, f, r, s, quote, apostrophe and backslash, plus octal escapes; 3.3 covers Unicode escapes before tokenization.

JLS SE 25, 14.20 The try statement: catch clauses are considered in order and the first whose type matches handles the exception; a catch clause that can never be reached because an earlier one catches a superclass is a compile-time error; alternatives in a multi-catch may not be subclasses of one another.
JLS SE 25, 14.20.2 Execution of try-finally and try-catch-finally: the finally block runs whether the try block and catch blocks complete normally or abruptly.

JLS SE 25, 14.20.3 try-with-resources: resources are closed in the reverse order in which they were initialized; catch and finally clauses of an extended try-with-resources run after the resources are closed.
Dev.java, Catching and Handling Exceptions: try, catch and finally blocks; the try-with-resources statement and AutoCloseable.
Java SE 25 API, AutoCloseable.close: called automatically on exiting a try-with-resources block for which the object has been declared in the resource specification header.
Java SE 25 API, Runtime.exit: "An invocation of this method never returns normally" (System.exit delegates to it), so a pending finally block does not run; observed on OpenJDK 25.0.4.1.
